questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical skills in runtime security, policy-as-code, and service-mesh identity to enforce tenant isolation at the API layer.

## Key Concepts
- SPIFFE/SVID identities for CNFs
- OPA Gatekeeper policy as code
- Namespace-scoped Istio/Linkerd authorization
- Cross-tenant API access controls

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8stenantaccess
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sTenantAccess
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8stenantaccess
      violation["deny"] { 
        input.review.object.kind == "Request" 
      }
```
```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sTenantAccess
spec:
  allowedTenants: ["tenantA"]
```
```yaml
# One-namespace manifest (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
```
```bash
# Verification (bash)
kubectl apply -f constraint.yaml
kubectl apply -f tenant-a-namespace.yaml
kubectl get constraints
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle key revocation and policy drift across tenants?
- How would you test policy performance at scale?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design multi-tenant upgrade workflows with strict rollback mechanisms and metric-driven canary promotion—a common production CNF pattern at scale.

## Key Concepts
- Canary deployments per-tenant using Istio or Linkerd for traffic splitting
- TenantUpgradePolicy CRD design for declarative upgrade management
- Metric-driven promotion windows with Prometheus and SLO definitions
- Safe rollback capabilities with idempotent manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantUpgradePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-upgrade
spec:
  tenantId: tenant-a
  targetVersion: v2.1.0
  canaryTrafficPercent: 5
  promotionCriteria:
    latencyThresholdMs: 100
    errorRateThresholdPercent: 0.5
    observationWindowMinutes: 10
  rollbackConfig:
    autoRollbackOnFailure: true
    maxRetries: 3
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical knowledge of cross-tenant isolation using runtime attestation (SPIRE) and policy enforcement (OPA) in CNF meshes. It assesses understanding of real-world challenges including tenant scoping, short-lived credential management, and gateway security enforcement.

## Key Concepts
- SPIRE workload attestation and SVID binding to tenant ID
- OPA/Rego policy enforcement for tenant isolation
- Service mesh RBAC, namespaces, and tenant-scoped ServiceAccounts
- End-to-end testing within a single namespace

## Code Example
```yaml
# SPIRE Attestation
apiVersion: spire.spiffe.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterSPIFFEID
metadata:
  name: cnf-workload
spec:
  spiffeIDTemplate: "spiffe://example.com/ns/{namespace}/tenant/{tenant_id}"
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf
  tenantIDLabel: "tenant.id"
---
# OPA Authorization Policy
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-gateway-policy
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: istio-ingressgateway
  action: CUSTOM
  provider:
    name: opa
  rules:
  - when:
    - key: request.headers[x-spire-attestation]
      notValues: ["invalid"]
    - key: request.headers[x-tenant-capability]
      values: ["tenant-a-read", "tenant-a-write"]
---
# Test Manifest (single namespace)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: cnf-workload
  namespace: tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant.id: "tenant-a"
    tenant.capability: "read,write"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: cnf-api
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  selector:
    app: cnf
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: tenantegress
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: TenantEgressConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |-
      package tenantegress

      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.kind == "EgressRule"
        tenant := input.review.object.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.tenants[tenant].allowlist
        dest := input.review.object.spec.destination
        not dest in allowed
        msg := sprintf("destination %v not allowed for tenant %v", [dest, tenant])
      }
```
```yaml
# Gatekeeper Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: TenantEgressConstraint
metadata:
  name: allowlist-tenantA
```
```yaml
# Kyverno example policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-egress-allowlist
spec:
  rules:
  - name: check-allowed-dest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["EgressRule"]
    validate:
      message: "Destination not allowed for tenant"
      pattern:
        spec.destination: "*"
```

- **Fail-Secure**: The `default allow = false` ensures requests are denied by default unless explicitly permitted
